preamble: Weakening of the palatal nasal stop [ɲ] to a palatal glide removes the oral closure while keeping the palatal place; in the best-documented case the nasality survives on the glide and on the preceding vowel, giving a nasalized approximant [j̃]. Brazilian and Angolan Portuguese realize 'nh' this way. Other well-documented cases are hard to find, so the change counts as rare.

examples.note: In Brazil and Angola the consonant written nh is realized as a nasal palatal approximant [j̃], which nasalizes the preceding vowel.
